channel.title: Stand to Reason – Bias and Credibility - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Stand to Reason – Bias and Credibility (str.org)

item.title: What to Say When Challenged to “Love and Accept” Like Jesus
item.description: If you’re asked the question “Doesn’t Jesus teach we should love and accept one another?” beware of naively affirming it, for two reasons. Greg Koukl explains.

item.title: Is a Changed Life Evidence for the Truth of Christianity?
item.description: A changed life is certainly noteworthy, but it’s not necessarily noble, so before one can know if it’s evidence of the truth of a religion, there’s a more pressing question that needs to be answered.

item.title: Seven Truths to Help You Prepare for Suffering
item.description: Since none of us will escape this life without suffering, here are seven truths from a new book by Clay and Jean E. Jones to help you prepare for what’s ahead.

item.title: Is God in Your Life?
item.description: The culture tells you that you are autonomous; you are in control; you can be whoever you want, so why are depression, anxiety, and suicide at historic highs? Here’s why autonomy is not the key to human flourishing.

item.title: Rapid Fire – Part 4
item.description: Greg continues his “rapid-fire” responses to common objections to Christianity, addressing claims that one is a good person, the need to see a miracle to believe in God, the illusion of consciousness, the inevitability of mistakes from human biblical authors, abortion protecting unwanted children, evidence vs. faith, and more.

item.title: Fishy Reasons to Deny the Sex Binary
item.description: Some transgender ideology advocates use examples from other species as evidence that sex is on a spectrum for human beings. Alan Shlemon explains why this kind of argument fails.

item.title: The Gospels Aren’t Myths
item.description: C.S. Lewis—a medieval and Renaissance literature scholar who was quite familiar with myths, legends, allegories, romances, etc.—explains his conviction that the Gospels are not myths.

item.title: Evangelism Is Not a Thing You Do
item.description: Evangelism is not something you do only if you feel specially called. If you are a Christian, you are already sent. But here’s why that shouldn’t scare you.

item.title: Give Greg a Call Tuesday
item.description: Call the podcast with your questions and challenges for Greg during the live program, 4:00 to 5:00 p.m. (PT), at (855) 243-9975. Outside the U.S., call (562) 424-8229.

item.title: No One Suffers More than One Person’s Pain
item.description: When trying to make sense of how our perfectly good, wise, and powerful God can coexist with all the evil and suffering in the world, we can easily be overwhelmed by looking at all evil all at once, but that is not a fair way of looking at the issue.

item.title: How to Navigate the Slippery Slope
item.description: Slippery slope arguments link one way of thinking to an unintended consequence that’s likely to follow. Some such appeals are faulty, but some are valid. Here’s the difference.
